messages:
eli: FYI — after the kernel selector change rolled last night, I'm seeing ~12–18% p95 increase on host-side for gRPC streaming at batch sizes ~1-4 and seq_len 512. Looks like extra allocs in pretoken parse path.
sara: Can you paste the trace? which host/region? @maria please peek if you have time.
eli: us-east-1 hostpool-a. Trace: perf + flamegraph snippet below. Noticed allocator churn in parse_shim::deserialize and grpc_writev staging.
maria: Got it. Initial skim — kselector now prefers avx_fused kernel for 512; dispatcher forces copy->aligned buffer in proxy path. That maps to the allocs.
noah: Do we have a repro script? I can run locally with --simulate-streaming to surface mem stats.
eli: repro: ./bench_stream --seq=512 --batch=1 --qps=1000 --proto=grpc2
Quick perf output:
```
host_parse_ms: 4.8 -> 5.7 (+18%)
kvcache_hot_miss: +2.3%
grpc_writev_calls: +1 per request
mallocs: +3200/s
```
maria: Hmm. KV cache miss uptick might be from different framing size changing cache key boundaries. Also AVX kernel needs contiguous buffer which forces a copy.
sara: Possible mitigations: 1) revert kernel selector for streaming small batches; 2) implement proxy buffer-pool to avoid temp allocs; 3) tweak batching heuristic to prefer kernel match based on seq_len distribution per-route.
noah: I'll prototype a buffer-pool patch in proxy that reuses pre-allocated iovecs and runs a microbench.
eli: Also seeing grpc path increase in writev count — might be fragmentation. Coalescing frames earlier should reduce syscalls + alloc churn.
maria: I'll run a kernel-selector sim that prefers non-avx for seq<=640 on streaming routes and compare. If perf recovers, we should encode selector heuristics per-route.
sara: @perf-bot can you schedule a quick canary with selector tweak + buffer-pool patch? Need a 2hr window.
perf-bot: Canary scheduled on us-east1-canary between 16:00-18:00 today. Notifying oncall.
eli: Thanks. I'll attach full flamegraph and raw perf logs to the canary ticket.
noah: Note — any selector rule changes must have a rollback guard and be behind a feature flag. Avoid global swap without fallback.
maria: Agreed. I'll open a PR with benchmarks, microbench harness, and spec for the selector gates; will link here.
eli: TL;DR: kernel choice + framing -> extra copies/allocs -> p95 bump. Next: buffer-pool (noah), selector tweak (maria), canary (perf-bot), rollback guard (sara).
